0.0.n: Here it introduces the closing remarks rather than answering a question.

0.2.n: With の動画, it refers to the current video.

0.3.n: Links 今回 to 動画, identifying which video is meant.

0.4.n: The speaker asks about the video the viewer has just watched.

0.6.n: お adds respect to the noun form of 楽しむ in this polite expression.

0.7.n: いただけました is past polite いただける; でしょう softens the question about the viewer's enjoyment.

0.8.n: Ends the sentence as a polite question.

1.0.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

1.2.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

1.4.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

1.7.n: A polite ending used here while introducing the channel as the topic.

1.8.n: Makes the introduction conversational and invites the listener's attention.

1.10.n: Needs な before a noun; here it describes the range of board games.

1.11.n: Connects 様々 to the noun ボードゲーム.

1.12.n: Japanese nouns do not need a plural ending.

1.13.n: Links ボードゲーム to 話題, specifying what the topics concern.

1.14.n: Refers to the board-game subjects covered by the channel.

1.15.n: Marks 話題 as what the channel delivers.

1.16.n: お plus the noun form of 届ける combines with する to humbly describe providing content.

1.17.n: しております is a humble, polite version of しています, describing the channel's ongoing activity.

2.0.n: The name of the video platform.

2.1.n: Links YouTube to 方 in a softened topic introduction.

2.2.n: 方 is conversational padding here, not a literal direction or person.

2.3.n: Marks YouTubeの方 as the topic.

2.4.n: Part of ですね, used here as polite conversational padding.

2.5.n: Helps hold the listener's attention while the speaker introduces the explanation.

2.7.n: Combines with 登録 to mean subscribing to a channel.

2.8.n: 登録 means registration; with チャンネル, it refers to subscribing.

2.9.n: Connects チャンネル登録 to 方, which adds conversational softness.

2.10.n: 方 adds indirectness here without changing the basic request to subscribe.

2.11.n: Marks チャンネル登録の方 as the action requested with する.

2.12.n: The て-form of する connects subscribing to いただけます, presenting it as a favor.

2.13.n: Polite いただける follows a て-form to describe receiving someone's action as a favor.

2.14.n: Introduces the consequence of subscribing to the channel.

2.16.n: The speaker refers to himself using a neutral, polite personal pronoun.

2.17.n: Marks 私 as the person uploading the video.

2.18.n: Refers to a future video uploaded by the speaker.

2.19.n: Connects 動画 to the softening word 方.

2.20.n: 方 is padding here; 動画の方 refers simply to the video.

2.21.n: Marks 動画の方 as what the speaker uploads.

2.22.n: Polite past of 登録する; before 時, it marks completion of uploading, even in a future situation.

2.23.n: The preceding clause specifies the occasion: once the speaker has uploaded a video.

2.24.n: Marks the upload time as when the notification happens.

2.26.n: Refers back to the new upload or news of it.

2.27.n: Marks それ as what can be communicated in the following ability expression.

2.28.n: Part of ですね, a spoken filler inserted before continuing the explanation.

2.29.n: Keeps the listener engaged during the speaker's pause.

2.31.n: 素早い changes its final い to く to describe how the news is communicated.

2.32.n: お plus the noun form of 伝える makes the expression courteous.

2.33.n: After お伝え, it expresses the ability to inform the viewer.

2.34.n: In できるようになる, よう refers to a state where something is possible.

2.35.n: Links よう to なる, marking the resulting state.

2.36.n: なっております is humble and polite なっている, describing the system's established arrangement.

2.37.n: Gives the reason for the subscription request that follows.

3.0.n: Adds warm encouragement and emphasis to the request.

3.1.n: Combines with 登録 to refer to a channel subscription.

3.2.n: The action being requested; チャンネル登録 is the usual expression for subscribing.

3.3.n: Connects チャンネル登録 to the softening word 方.

3.4.n: 方 makes the request indirect; the object marker を is omitted after it.

3.6.n: お願い combines with いたします to form a courteous request.

3.7.n: The polite form of いたす, a humble alternative to する.

4.0.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

4.2.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

4.4.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

4.6.n: Identifies the channel the speaker belongs to.

4.7.n: Links the channel to Haru99, indicating affiliation.

4.9.n: The name portion of the speaker's username Haru99.

4.10.n: The numeric portion of the username Haru99, not a separate quantity.

4.12.n: The first portion of でした, the polite past form of です.

4.13.n: Completes でした; the past form serves as a conventional sign-off.

0.lit: Well, this time's video, were you able to enjoy it?
0.tip: お楽しみいただけましたでしょうか is a very polite way to ask whether the viewer enjoyed the video.

1.lit: The Game Gallery channel, you know, we are delivering topics concerning various board games.
1.tip: お届けしております humbly describes the channel's regular activity, rather than one delivery happening right now.

2.lit: Regarding YouTube, if you kindly subscribe, when I upload videos, that can quickly be communicated, because it is arranged so.
2.tip: The repeated の方 softens the speaker's phrasing but adds little meaning; it does not indicate a direction here.

3.lit: By all means, channel subscription, I humbly request.
3.tip: お願いいたします is a humble, more formal alternative to お願いします.

4.lit: It was Haru99 of The Game Gallery channel.
4.tip: でした is commonly used when signing off, even though the speaker's identity has not changed.
